metaDescription: Six countertop ice makers at or below $200, led by nugget machines, compared on daily output, tank size, ice texture and upkeep for home use.
expertTake: The EUHOMY 34 lb nugget maker with a handle is the best pick because it combines soft chewable ice, a six-minute first batch and a portable body. The hOmeLabs bullet maker is the value pick when you want two cube sizes without the nugget premium. Anyone who only wants ice for the occasional drink should skip this price tier and buy a bullet machine for less.
introParagraphs: With a larger budget, the main upgrade in a countertop ice maker is the type of ice. Nugget machines freeze a layer of water on a cold cylinder, scrape it off with an auger and press it into soft, airy pellets. People who chew ice or order fountain drinks prefer that texture.

Nugget makers also run louder, weigh more and need more cleaning than bullet makers. Whether the premium is worth it depends on how much you enjoy the ice itself. Every machine below was at or under $200 on its listing when this guide was updated, and prices move, so check the live page.

products.name: EUHOMY 34 lb Nugget Ice Maker with Handle
products.description:
This EUHOMY makes soft, airy nugget ice in as little as six minutes, which is quick for the type. Nugget ice comes from an auger scraping a frozen layer off a cold cylinder, so the pellets are porous and absorb drink flavor. The 1.2 qt tank feeds the machine with a single button to start.

It is rated at 34 lb per day, a step above the 26 lb bullet machines, and the handle lets you carry it. The removable top cover simplifies cleaning. Next to the other EUHOMY nugget model it starts a minute faster, and next to the Frigidaire nugget V2 it quotes a much shorter first batch.

The auger adds noise beyond a compressor hum, so keep it out of a quiet bedroom. Descale the evaporator regularly and use filtered water. It is the all-round choice for a household that wants good ice every day, and the handle helps when you move it between the counter and a table.
products.bestFor: Households that love chewable ice and want a portable machine.
pros: Soft chewable nugget ice that takes on drink flavor
34 lb daily rating beats bullet machines
Built-in handle for moving it around
cons: Auger noise is louder than a bullet maker
Reservoir is small for long parties

products.name: EUHOMY 34 lb Nugget Pebble Ice Maker, 7 Minute
products.description:
This is the second EUHOMY nugget model, with a seven-minute first batch and a clear window to check the ice level. Operation is a single ICE button after you fill the tank, so there is nothing to learn. It uses the same freeze-and-scrape principle as the first model.

The 34 lb daily rating matches the handle version, but it is a plainer machine with a view window instead of the carry handle. Compared with the Kismile at 35 lb, the output is nearly the same, and compared with the Frigidaire V2 it is quicker to the first batch. The soft pebbles are easy to chew and suit blended drinks.

Expect some noise from the auger and compressor. Clean the reservoir and run a descaling cycle monthly in hard-water areas. It is a good pick when you want the nugget experience without paying for extras, and the window saves you from lifting the lid to check the bin.
products.bestFor: Anyone who wants nugget ice with a window to check the level.
pros: Soft pebble ice with a pleasant crunch
Clear window shows when the bin is full
cons: No carry handle on this version
Seven minutes to the first batch, one minute slower than its sibling

products.name: Kismile Stainless Nugget Ice Maker, 35 lb
products.description:
The Kismile has the highest rated output in the lineup at 35 lb per day, and a stainless steel body that looks more solid than plastic shells. It makes nugget ice, sometimes called sonic or pebble ice, from a 1.1L tank. A press of the power button starts a cleaning routine.

Output is only a pound above the EUHOMY models, so the difference is about build and finish. Compared with the EUHOMY with a handle, it has a smaller tank and lacks the handle. Compared with the Frigidaire V2, it shows a stronger daily rating and a more modern design.

A stainless body shows fingerprints, so keep a cloth nearby. The small tank means refilling during an evening of drinks. It is a good pick for a kitchen counter where appearance matters, provided you accept refilling the small tank a few times per gathering.
products.bestFor: Counter display where a stainless finish and top output matter.
pros: 35 lb daily rating tops the lineup
cons: Smallest tank in the nugget group at 1.1L
No carry handle and fingerprints show on stainless

products.name: Frigidaire Crunchy Nugget Ice Maker V2, 33 lb
products.description:
Frigidaire's nugget maker V2 aims at the restaurant-style crunch, with a gunmetal finish that looks at home beside modern appliances. It plugs into a standard outlet and works on a counter or at a campsite. The first ice appears in about fifteen minutes.

That start is slower than either EUHOMY model, and the rated 33 lb per day sits just below them. What you gain is a major appliance brand and a recognizable look. Compared with the Kismile, it offers less output, but compared with the bullet-style Frigidaire EFIC117 it makes softer ice.

The longer first batch matters if you need ice quickly before guests arrive, so start it early. Clean and descale on schedule, since nugget machines trap scale in the cylinder. It suits those who value brand support over speed, and it travels well to a lake house or campsite with an outlet.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a known appliance brand and restaurant-style crunch.
pros: Plugs into any outlet and travels to camp
Backed by an established appliance brand
cons: About fifteen minutes to the first ice
Rated output is slightly below the EUHOMY and Kismile

products.name: hOmeLabs Countertop Ice Maker, Two Ice Sizes
products.description:
The hOmeLabs is a bullet-ice maker, not a nugget machine, which makes it the odd one out here. It makes nine cubes in about six minutes and lets you choose between small bullet cubes for quick chilling and larger ones that melt more slowly. That choice helps when you fill coolers as well as glasses.

Its 26 lb daily rating trails the nugget machines by 7 to 9 lb, but the compact body is easy to place. Compared with the Frigidaire EFIC117, it adds the size option and a modern black finish. Compared with the nugget units, it makes harder, slower-melting ice and runs more quietly.

The self-cleaning function rinses the reservoir, though descaling still needs a separate step. It is the pick for people who want bullet ice flexibility at the lower end of this cap.
products.bestFor: Cooler and pitcher use where cube size flexibility matters.
pros: Two cube sizes for different jobs
Nine bullet cubes in about six minutes
cons: 26 lb daily rating is below the nugget group
Bullet ice is harder than nugget ice

products.name: Frigidaire EFIC117 Stainless Ice Maker, Copper
products.description:
The EFIC117 is a bullet-ice machine with a copper stainless finish that stands out from the usual black and silver. It makes nine bullet cubes every seven minutes or so and has a transparent window showing the ice level.

It is rated at 26 lb per day, the same class as the hOmeLabs, with a slightly longer cycle. Compared with the nugget machines it costs less to run and makes less noise but produces harder ice. Against the hOmeLabs it lacks the cube size choice but looks more distinctive.

Wipe the stainless with a soft cloth and descale periodically. It is a pick for style-minded buyers who want a branded bullet maker, and its quieter running suits an open-plan living area.
products.bestFor: Kitchens where a distinctive finish and a brand name matter.
pros: Transparent window to check ice level
cons: Seven-minute cycle is slower than some rivals
Hard bullet ice, not soft chewable ice

buyingCriteria.explanation: Nugget makers like the EUHOMY and Kismile produce soft, porous pellets, while bullet makers like the hOmeLabs and Frigidaire EFIC117 make harder cubes. Nugget absorbs drink flavor and is easy to chew. Bullet ice lasts longer in a cooler and runs quieter.
The Kismile claims 35 lb per day, the EUHOMY models 34 lb, the Frigidaire V2 33 lb and the bullet machines 26 lb. Those are best-case figures in a cool room. Real output drops in warm kitchens.

The EUHOMY with a handle quotes about 6 minutes and the other EUHOMY about 7, while the Frigidaire V2 needs about 15. After the first batch cycles are faster. If guests are arriving soon, start early.

The Kismile has a 1.1L tank and the EUHOMY has about 1.2 qt, so both need refilling during long sessions. Nugget machines use water quickly because they also drain melt water. Plan to top up before each evening, and keep a pitcher of filtered water next to the machine so the habit stays easy.

Nugget makers combine compressor hum with auger noise and a rattle of falling pellets. A bullet maker is quieter. Place a nugget machine away from sleeping areas and give it airflow, since a closed cabinet traps heat and cuts both output and compressor life.
Nugget cylinders trap minerals from hard water, which cuts output and flavor. Use filtered water and descale monthly or more. A self-clean button is no substitute.

specDecoder.meaning: Small, soft, porous pellets formed by scraping and compressing frozen water. They chew easily and cool quickly.
specDecoder.watchFor: The EUHOMY, Kismile and Frigidaire V2 make it, the hOmeLabs and EFIC117 do not.

specDecoder.meaning: A continuous-run ceiling in cool conditions, not a daily average. Warm rooms cut it.
specDecoder.watchFor: Nugget units claim 33 to 35 lb, bullet units 26 lb.

specDecoder.meaning: The reservoir that feeds the freezing cylinder. Small tanks demand frequent refills.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Kismile lists 1.1L, the EUHOMY about 1.2 qt.

specDecoder.meaning: A setting that changes the size of bullet cubes. Large cubes melt slower.
specDecoder.watchFor: Only the hOmeLabs offers it here.

specDecoder.meaning: A rotating screw that scrapes ice from the cylinder in nugget makers. It adds noise and a wear part.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ice type
howWeEvaluated.description: We separated nugget from bullet machines since the ice texture is the main reason to spend more. Four of the six picks make nugget or pebble ice. The hOmeLabs and EFIC117 were judged as bullet makers.

howWeEvaluated.title: Output and speed
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared daily ratings from 26 lb to 35 lb and first-batch times from 6 to 15 minutes. These are treated as ceilings, not measurements. The Frigidaire V2 was marked down on start time.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity and refill
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at tank volume since nugget machines consume water quickly. The Kismile and EUHOMY tanks are small. We favored models that make refilling simple.

howWeEvaluated.title: Build and finish
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared the Kismile's stainless body, the Frigidaire gunmetal and copper finishes, and the EUHOMY's handle. Appearance matters on a counter but was weighed below function.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed recurring owner themes such as auger noise and scale buildup, without quoting any rating figure. The $200 cap was applied against live listing position.

cards.label: Nugget ice
cards.text: Soft, chewable and flavor-absorbing, but louder and more demanding to clean. The EUHOMY, Kismile and Frigidaire V2 make it.

cards.label: Bullet ice
cards.text: Harder and slower melting, with quieter machines and less upkeep. The hOmeLabs and Frigidaire EFIC117 make it.

howToChoose.note: Choose nugget if you love chewing ice, and bullet if you want quiet and lower cost.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: True nugget or pebble ice from an auger machine, a tank big enough for your habit and a model that is easy to descale.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The EUHOMY 34 lb with Handle is the best balance of speed and portability. The Kismile gives the highest rated output.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want faster refills, a bigger tank and heavy daily use. Above this cap you find larger nugget units and under-counter machines.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You mostly want cold drinks. The hOmeLabs bullet maker costs less and does the job.

maintenance.why: Standing water breeds biofilm. A dry tank keeps pellets tasting clean.
Mineral buildup slows ice production and strains the auger. Use a maker-approved descaler or citric acid.
Handled surfaces pick up oils. Warm soapy water is enough.
Dust blocks compressor airflow. Wipe or vacuum them.
It flushes the water path but does not replace descaling.

faq.q: Is nugget ice worth the extra money?
faq.a: If you chew ice or drink iced coffee daily, yes. Nugget absorbs flavor and cools quickly, though bullet ice is fine for ordinary drinks.
This guide uses a $200 cap, and nugget machines sit toward the top of it. Prices move, so the cap reflects listing prices when the guide was updated.

faq.q: How long do nugget machines last?
faq.a: With regular descaling, many last for years. The auger and cylinder are the wear parts.
Louder than bullet machines because of the auger. Place them away from bedrooms.

faq.q: Can I leave ice in the bin?
faq.a: It melts slowly. Nugget machines drain melt water back, so scoop ice into a freezer bag for storage.
It is strongly advised in hard-water areas. Scale builds up in the cylinder and cuts output.
